gold_prose:
# Inference at Marin: who, where, current performance, and open issues

**Short version.** "Inference" at Marin is four overlapping things, with different owners and very different maturity:

1. **The serving substrate — the Iris inference service** (a vLLM-only distributed service that runs on the Iris cluster and hands evals/RL an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint via a `RunningModel` handoff). Owner: **Romain Yon (`yonromai`)**. The *handoff contract* and *brokered serving path* shipped in code; the *formal design doc went stale* and the older centralized-inference RFC was auto-closed stale. This is the layer the "brokered vLLM wedge" bug lives in.
2. **GrugMoE-in-vLLM enablement** (get Marin's own MoE to serve correctly on TPUs and GPUs). Owner: **Romain Yon**. TPU path **landed/closed**; GPU correctness **validated at EP8**; a July epic (#6867) tracks full-size + fast-enough work, **0/3 children closed**.
3. **RL rollout inference throughput** (make generation fast enough that RL isn't inference-bound). Epic owner: **Isaac Hodes (`ihodes`, #6709)**; the real load and the only concrete numbers come from **Benjamin Feuer (`penfever`)**'s MarinSkyRL. Still at the **"establish a baseline"** stage — no agreed H100 rollout-tok/s baseline or target exists.
4. **The role definition + two unbuilt components** — **#6500 "[Epic] Inference / Serving Infrastructure Specialist"** (penfever) charters an inference server, a **Format Library (#6626)** and an **Agent Harness (#6627)**; the latter two are **chartered but unstarted**.

The current performance evidence is thin and must be read carefully: the only headline number (**~2.5 hr per RL step, ~10M tokens generated/step, 64×H100**) is an **end-to-end RL step wall-clock, not a serving throughput**, and it was never decomposed into generation-vs-train.

---

## 1. Who is doing inference work (people map)

- **Romain Yon (`yonromai` / "romain")** — owns the **Iris inference service** end-to-end (RFC/design, MVP, the served-model handoff, the brokered serving path, the July Grug inference epic) and the **GrugMoE-in-vLLM** enablement on both TPU and GPU. Also the `vllm`/`tpu-inference` fork rebase tooling. [#5285](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5285), [#5400](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5400), [#5887](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5887), [#6867](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6867), [#6664](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6664)
- **Russell Power (`rjpower`)** — owns the underlying **Iris cluster/scheduler/federation** machinery, brought up the **CoreWeave `cw-us-east-02a` H100 cluster** ([#6293](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6293)), shipped the **`marin-serve` one-liner inference server** ([#6556](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6556)), and drove the "one vLLM fork" consolidation ([#7097](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/7097), per weekly summary).
- **Will Held (`Helw150`)** — the RL/rollout **consumer**: filed the original centralized-inference RFC ([#4401](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4401)), filed the serving-reliability "wedge" bug (#6983), and added inference-side **logit-mixing** plumbing (a brokered teacher/student mixed-logit `RunningModel`, #7113, per summary).
- **Benjamin Feuer (`penfever` = `@benjaminfeuer`)** — owns **MarinSkyRL** RL-inference bring-up on GPUs (131k-context RL on MoE models), where the current real inference *load* and *throughput* numbers come from; also authored the role-definition epic. [#6335](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6335), [#6629](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6629), [#6655](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6655), [#6656](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6656), [#6218](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6218), [#6500](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6500)
- **David Hall (`dlwh`)** — owns **Levanter-side inference** (the JAX reference path and the TPU RL-rollout backend-parity epic), and made Levanter inference ~10× faster. [#6227](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6227)
- **AlienKevin** — prior **async-RL perf** lead: the "Benchmark and speed up async RL" work ([#2237](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2237)) and the SWE-ZERO rollout-throughput work ([#4719](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4719)).
- **Rohith Kuditipudi** — carries **TPU vLLM fork overlay patches**; hit the RPA-v3 v4 gap (#7085) and lm-eval pin rot (per summary).
- **Isaac Hodes (`ihodes`)** — owns the tracking/def-of-done issues for **evals-on-Iris** ([#5368](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5368)) and the **rollout-speed epic** ([#6709](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6709)), and scoped the **Format Library** ([#6626](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6626)) and **Agent Harness** ([#6627](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6627)).
- **Iris consumers / stakeholders** for a shared inference service: Michael Ryan, moojink, XenonMolecule, Mrinal Kumar, Ahmed M Ahmed (per the #inference / RFC threads).

### The role charter: #6500 (defined, not demonstrably filled)

**[#6500 "[Epic] Inference / Serving Infrastructure Specialist"](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6500)** (penfever, 2026-06-18) is the *public definition* of who owns inference — "what it owns, the boundary with the supervisor + the managers it serves, its current near-term work, and its compute envelope." It charters the role around three components: a **Marin Inference Server** (a thin patch on vLLM), a **Marin Format Library** (scoped as #6626), and a **Marin Agent Harness** (scoped as #6627). penfever authored it as one of a set of parallel role-charters the same day; the corpus contains no evidence the slot has been filled by a single named contributor — the actual inference-server work is being realized ad hoc by **yonromai** (GrugMoE vLLM), **rjpower** (`marin-serve`), and **dlwh** (Levanter). Treat #6500 as a role *definition*, not tracked execution.

*(Caveat: the frozen corpus stores issue bodies truncated to their opening ~250 chars and exposes no assignee/state metadata, so "unfilled/unstarted" is inferred from empty threads and the absence of linked implementation PRs, not from an explicit field.)*

---

## 2. Where it's at, by subsystem

### 2a. The Iris inference service (the serving substrate) — Romain Yon

Iris proper is the Ray-like actor/scheduler substrate (actors run on worker VMs inside the cluster VPC; external clients reach them via an actor-proxy route — [#4109](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4109)). The **inference service** is a distributed vLLM serving layer built on top of it that exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint to power evals (and later RL rollouts / synthetic data). Chronology and current state:

| Item | What | State (in corpus) |
|---|---|---|
| [#4401](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4401) | RFC: **Centralized Low-Priority Inference Service on Iris** (Will Held, Claude-drafted) — multi-model, for data-curation/RL/synth | **Auto-closed stale 2026-07-04** (inactive 83 days). Superseded by Romain's eval-first design. |
| [#5368](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5368) | Tracking: **Inference service for evals** (ihodes). DoD: selected evals run on Iris in a **worker-preemption-resilient** way (preemption blows up jobs today); **decided: use vLLM** | Continued into June via #6042/#6041. |
| [#4841](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/4841) | RFC 01 — **Decouple evals from model backends via OpenAI-compatible HTTP** | **Draft PR** (stacked on #4815). |
| [#5285](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5285) | RFC: **Served Model Eval Handoff** — introduces the `RunningModel` handoff object between serving code and eval code; `lm_eval` first consumer | **Merged** — the landed backbone evals call. |
| [#5351](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5351) | [codex] Iris inference routing **MVP/prototype** | **Closed 2026-05-04** as a prototype ("use the findings as design evidence"). |
| [#5400](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5400) | **Design Iris inference service** — vLLM-only; Iris owns vLLM lifecycle, readiness, **request brokering**, cleanup, diagnostics | **Went stale 2026-06-07** (23 days inactive). The formal design never got ratified. |
| [#5887](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/5887) | **Broker vLLM HumanEval serving across Iris TPU workers** — one eval fans out across multiple TPU vLLM workers; **broker leases** so a preempted worker only loses its in-flight lease | Built and reviewed (rjpower); the concrete "request brokering" implementation. |

**Net status:** the *handoff contract* (`RunningModel` + OpenAI-HTTP, #5285) is **landed**; the *brokered vLLM serving path* (#5887, broker/proxy/worker) is **built and in use**; but the *formal design doc* (#5400) **went stale** and the older centralized-inference RFC (#4401) was **closed stale**. Iris-as-a-service is real in code but its design was never ratified. Note also that a June control-plane hiccup — [#6754](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6754), "Iris EndpointService 404 in brokered smoke" — was an **API mismatch, not a serving regression** (resolved after rjpower restarted the cluster with an endpoint-API update).

### 2b. GrugMoE-in-vLLM enablement — Romain Yon

- **TPU serving — landed and closed.** GrugMoE inference on TPU via the Marin-owned `vllm`/`tpu-inference` forks **closed as completed on 2026-07-02** (#6041), landing in **[#6664](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6664)** with the export path, fork pins, and a real-checkpoint v6e e2e test comparing vLLM against the Levanter/JAX reference. [#6041 close comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6041#issuecomment-4869501446)
- **GPU serving — correctness validated at EP8.** The GPU support issue **[#6042](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6042)** (DoD: "loaded and used for inference in vLLM on GPUs; correctness tested, perf okay for evals"; **RL-grade perf explicitly out of scope**) **closed** after **eight-way expert-parallel (EP8)** serving of a real GrugMoE checkpoint passed on CoreWeave/H100. Validation was Romain's draft harness **[#6891](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6891)** (real checkpoint, TP1/DP8/EP8 on 8×H100 CoreWeave, matched a JAX/Levanter reference; short greedy parity + expert coverage only, performance/long-run deferred), restacked as **[#6966](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6966)** after an XSA/GQA attention-sharding fix (#6965). Per the weekly summary, **Isaac Hodes logged the EP8-passed close** on #6042.
- **July epic — [#6867](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6867)** (yonromai, 2026-07-02): "Support full size GrugMoE model on both TPUs and GPUs. Stretch: Inference is fast enough on GPUs." Children: **#6868** (TPU correctness), **[#6869](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6869)** (correctness on largest checkpoint, GPUs), **[#6870](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6870)** (GPU throughput for RL). **0/3 closed** as of the week it opened. The forks pull from **`marin-community/vllm` + `tpu-inference`** (confirmed by the #6664/#6966 pins).
- **`marin-serve`** — [#6556](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/6556) (rjpower): a one-liner to boot vLLM on an Iris TPU slice (HF model or `gs://` checkpoint) with a small browser dashboard. This is the "patch on vLLM" inference-server component in practice, built independently of the #6500 role.

### 2c. RL rollout inference (MarinSkyRL) — Benjamin Feuer / penfever

MarinSkyRL is the live consumer generating real inference load. It has **migrated across clusters over time — do not attribute all of it to one chip/cluster**:

- **MoE R3/TIS bring-up (June) = JSC Jupiter, GH200.** **[#6335](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6335)** "Stand up router replay (R3) and TIS on MarinSkyRL" (penfever) is on **JSC J[upiter]**, Qwen3-Next-A3B family. The **GH200 device-pinning** issue (Ray no longer overriding `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` via `RAY_ACCEL_ENV_VAR_OVERRIDE_ON_ZERO`, so policy ranks collided on GPU-0) is a **Jupiter/GH200 artifact**, fixed with per-node local-rank pinning. Proof-of-life: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, EP4×FSDP4, grouped-GEMM + TIS, **JSC Jupiter job 849580**, ran ~12 h to walltime timeout on **6 nodes (24× GH200)**. The 80B bring-up also ran on Jupiter GH200 ([#6655](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6655) retro). **This is GH200, not CoreWeave H100.**
- **CoreWeave H100 workflow (June) = `cw-us-east-02a`.** **[#6629](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6629)** validated the gang-scheduled multi-node MarinSkyRL workflow on the **CoreWeave `cw-us-east-02a` H100** cluster via Iris (1-node 8×H100 and 2-node 16×H100 smokes end-to-end).
- **131k / CP+DCP (June) = multi-cluster.** [#6656](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6656) is the CP/DCP + 131k long-context RL campaign retro.
- **Current state (July): "131k RL on MoEs (MarinSkyRL) is plumbed on CoreWeave."** Per Feuer's Discord and the weekly summary, Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B each **fit on 64×H100 (8 nodes)** on CoreWeave. The tracking issue for this (#7052) is **not in the frozen corpus**.
- **Two vLLM forks, two owners.** GrugMoE *serving* uses **`marin-community/vllm`** (+ `tpu-inference`). The **RL/MarinSkyRL** track pulls from a **separate `mlfoundations/vllm` fork, `penfever/working` branch** — Feuer, 2026-07-14 #inference: "did you already merge the active branch features in from `github.com/mlfoundations/vllm` `penfever/working`? … I won't be able to do RL until we sync up on the vLLM branch + fork." In that same thread Feuer points to a follow-up issue (#7164, not itself in the frozen corpus) for adding a training `GrugMoeForCausalLM` PyTorch modeling class so GrugMoE can load into MarinSkyRL.

### 2d. Format Library (#6626) and Agent Harness (#6627) — chartered, unstarted

- **[#6626](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6626) "Marin format library for chat/response"** (ihodes): a single Python module that is the **authoritative source of truth for chat/response format in BOTH directions — RENDER a conversation → exact token string, and PARSE model output → structured `{reasoning / tool_calls / final / tool_results}`** (the "cheap ~80%" of `openai-harmony`/`mistral-common`; round-trip `parse(render(x)) == x` tested). **Not started** in corpus; the only render-side code that exists is Levanter's one-way Jinja chat-template rendering (dlwh: #6342, #1876) — the parse half doesn't exist. Blocked on the undecided Stage-4 chat-template ("likely Qwen-style") choice; explicitly punt-able to 2027.
- **[#6627](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6627) "Agent harness for agentic RL"** (ihodes): a harness that interfaces with Marin's inference solution, with strong malformed-tool-call failure-mode detection, a built-in LLM judge, a fixed tool set, dedicated Web-Fetch/Web-Search endpoints, and WYSIWYG trace extraction (so SFT works); a terminus-2-style sidecar. **Not started** in corpus; current agentic-RL work uses stopgaps (mini-swe-agent / Harbor / terminus-2, e.g. AlienKevin's SWE-ZERO #4719).

---

## 3. Current performance (every number labeled + hardware attached)

- **RL step time (MarinSkyRL, achieved, but NOT a serving throughput):** Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B each fit on **64×H100 (8 nodes), CoreWeave**, at **~2.5 hr/step** generating **~10M tokens/step**, at **131k context**. Feuer's words: *"~2.5hr / step at the moment which is slower than I would like but not insane."* **This is an end-to-end async-RL step wall-clock** (inference passes + gather + train), **not** an isolated tok/s. Russell Power explicitly asked Feuer to decompose it — "what performance we're seeing from the training side" — and got only a token *count* ("~10M tokens generated per step"), **never a generation-vs-train time split**. 131k is context length ("probably the limit of this hardware without additional cleverness"), not throughput. The incoming 80B-scale model (Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B) is **projected** to need **96–128×H100**. [Discord 2026-07-09](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1524748716190339122/1524749076355088485)
- **TPU Levanter reference vs vLLM (achieved):** dlwh's Levanter-inference optimization made it **~10× faster**, landing **within ~12% of vLLM-TPU** — "good enough for evals," but vLLM is still wanted and is "probably a hard requirement for SkyRL." [#6041](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6041#issuecomment-4869501446)
- **GPU GrugMoE serving (achieved):** correctness at **EP8 passed** on 8×H100 CoreWeave (short greedy parity + expert coverage). The DoD for #6042 was only "perf okay (good enough for evals)"; **serious/RL-grade perf is out of scope there** and deferred to #6870, whose "fast enough" DoD is still a literal **TODO** ("Within X% of Jax on GPUs vs. within Y% of reference model"). [#6042](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6042), [#6870](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6870)
- **No H100/GH200 isolated inference baseline exists.** The rollout-speed epic **#6709** makes "measure and document the current serving baseline" its explicit **first, not-yet-done task**; there is **no agreed rollout-tok/s baseline and no target**. [#6709](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6709)

### The measured throughput baselines that DO exist (all TPU/A100 — the natural build-on for #6709)

The epic's "no baseline" framing is literally true *for H100 rollout tok/s*, but understates a body of real, quantified prior work that #6709 should build on:

- **#2237 (AlienKevin, closed):** on **TPU v5p-8, Llama-3.1-8B**, "3.7× RL **training** speed up from 4.1 → 15.4 requests/s." **Caveat: this is a *trainer* number, not rollout inference** — the actor/rollout side was already ~3× faster (~13 req/s) and was not the thing sped up. Do not present it as a generation baseline. [#2237](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/2237)
- **#4719 (AlienKevin, SWE-ZERO):** **3.4× per-worker rollout throughput** from `--enable-prefix-caching` alone (600 → 4,600 rollouts/batch/hr) on **vLLM/TPU v6e-4**, with vLLM prefill+decode+queue = 84.6% of the per-rollout budget. [#4719](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4719)
- **#6227 epic / #6229 / #6230 (dlwh, TPU Levanter-vs-vLLM decode parity — the cleanest rollout-generation numbers in corpus):** on **v6e-8, TP8, `prefill_b8_i2048_o128_n1`**, vLLM **~1212–1264 decode tok/s** vs Levanter **~899–958** (ratio ~0.74–0.76, target FAIL); on **v5p-8, TP4, `mixed_b32_i512_o512_n1`**, vLLM **5215 decode** vs Levanter **3131** (ratio 0.60, FAIL). **#6709 links none of these.** [#6227](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6227), [#6229](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6229), [#6230](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6230)
- **#6218 (penfever, the richest GPU RL grid):** MarinSkyRL non-agentic throughput ablations on **CINECA Leonardo, A100-64GB** — effective-tokens/s sweeps, CUDA-graphs and seq-len knobs, generation-vs-train boundedness analysis. **A100, not H100.** [#6218](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6218)

The mismatch is (a) **hardware** — every measured baseline is TPU or A100, while #6709 targets H100 — and (b) **mis-linking** — #6709 links #2237 (a *trainer* number) but not the genuinely-relevant rollout-parity work. What #6709 uniquely still lacks is the **H100 port** of measurement that already exists elsewhere.

---

## 4. Open issues / risks

- **#6709 (rollout-speed epic):** open; **no baseline documented, no perf target agreed**. The whole speed track hinges on this. [#6709](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6709)
- **#6870 (GPU GrugMoE perf "decent"):** open; DoD is an unquantified **TODO**. [#6870](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6870)
- **#6869 (full-size GrugMoE GPU correctness):** open — EP8 passed on *a* checkpoint, but the *largest*-checkpoint correctness bar remains. [#6869](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6869)
- **#6983 (brokered vLLM "wedge") — resolved, but with a caveat.** Will Held's reproducible wedge turned out to be a **model/serving bug, not a broker bug**: fast vLLM HTTP 400s once the prompt crossed **marin-8b-base's true 4096-token position limit** (`Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan`, masked by `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN` + an oversized `max_model_len`); Romain Yon's instrumented rerun measured the **broker/proxy path clean** (`dropped_responses=0`, `rejected_requests=0`), and Will withdrew the reproduction claim. **But the *original field wedge* (brokered clients stalling >30 min against an idle, healthy engine, no restarts) "remains genuine but unreproduced,"** and the silent NaN-400 was flagged as possibly deserving its own issue. So the broker was exonerated *on the reproduced case only*. (Body not in frozen corpus; narrated by the 2026-07-06/07-12 weekly summary.) [summary](https://mws.oa.dev/summaries/summary-2026-07-06_2026-07-12.html)
- **#7117 (vLLM-compatible BF16 HF export regression):** **open** — the 134 GB / 39-shard export verified by whole-tree SHA256, but reruns of the inference assertion hit an **NCCL `ncclAlltoAll` error** on the JIT path. [summary](https://mws.oa.dev/summaries/summary-2026-07-06_2026-07-12.html)
- **#7085 (TPU RPA v3):** ragged-paged-attention v3 raises `NotImplementedError: Unsupported tpu_version=4` on v4-8 workers, so Rohith Kuditipudi **can't run inference there at all**; minimal fix is a `case 4` fallback in the block-size heuristic. [summary](https://mws.oa.dev/summaries/summary-2026-07-06_2026-07-12.html)
- **`marin-serve` GPU gaps:** #7111/#7133 (`marin-serve --gpu` can't boot vLLM cleanly — TPU/GPU extras and torch pins collide; the per-job `uvx` workaround still needs a real H100 boot test) and #7106/#7107 (`marin-serve` fails cryptically outside a workspace checkout). [summary](https://mws.oa.dev/summaries/summary-2026-07-06_2026-07-12.html)
